transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Redwood: Samira Patel, Diego Ramos, Lina Novak
Customer: Maya Chen, Owen Rao, Priya Singh, Ethan Cole

Summary: Align SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), scope benchmark shapes and traffic, produce pilot runbook and acceptance criteria.

Topics covered: success criteria, workload sizing, p95/p99 definitions, measurement harness, timeline.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Maya (SummitScale): hi, maya here.
[00:00:07] Owen: owen here.
[00:00:08] Priya: priya here.
[00:00:09] Ethan: ethan here.
[00:00:12] Diego (Redwood SE): diego here, will focus on perf / measurement.
[00:00:15] Lina (CSM): lina on for ops and timeline.
[00:00:20] Samira: awesome. objective today is to scope the POC so we can validate latency targets — specifically we want to align on when TTFT matters vs TPOT and what p95/p99 buckets you care about. also capture traffic shapes.
[00:00:38] Maya: high level — we have a conversational search feature that returns a short answer, and a longer summarization job used internally. the conversational path usually returns 1-3 tokens of system prefix then ~40 tokens of response. the summarization path is 400-800 tokens output.
[00:00:58] Samira: ok so two distinct classes: short-chat and long-batch summaries, got it. what's your SLA expectation? pitch us something realistic.
[00:01:08] Priya: for chat we want 95th < 150ms TTFT ideally, p99 < 350ms. for long summaries we don't have strict TTFT but total per-request completion latency (end-to-end) should be < 4s at p95 for 800-token summaries. is that doable?
[00:01:28] Diego: that p95 150ms TTFT is aggressive but potentially achievable on dedicated GPU pools with warm KV and minimal batching. for hosted/shared, you'd likely see higher TTFT at p95 without prewarmed workers. p99 is often where things jump due to cold starts and queueing.
[00:01:48] Maya: question — we saw some vendors quote per-token latency numbers; how do you suggest we reason about TPOT vs TTFT?
[00:01:56] Diego: good question. define terms first: TTFT = time-to-first-token, primarily impacted by model load, kernel selection, attention warmup, and any routing/fallback. TPOT (we used shorthand) is the sustained per-token time once generation is streaming — think tokens/sec. TTFT matters for perceived latency for chat (first reply), TPOT matters for long outputs and throughput/cost.
[00:02:20] Samira: right — and our recommendation is to set both SLOs but weight them per traffic class. short-chat: TTFT p95/p99 primary; long-batch: TPOT and end-to-end p95. we also advise slice by prompt length and by presence of KV cache hits.
[00:02:37] [00:02:40] Owen: what about batching? our workload is high concurrency, will batching help or hurt TTFT?
[00:02:47] Diego: batching increases TPOT efficiency (lower cost per token) but can increase TTFT because requests wait for batch window. Redwood runtime allows dynamic batching thresholds and latency SLOs — you can set max latency per request and the runtime will cut through batching if needed. in the POC we can test with a low-latency config (small batch, immediate dispatch) vs high-throughput config (batch size 8-16).
[00:03:12] Maya: cool. for the POC we want to see both modes and understand cost tradeoffs. can you produce a simulation that shows expected token throughput and cost per request for our mix?
[00:03:22] Diego: yes, i'll produce a simulation spreadsheet that inputs your token distribution and concurrency and outputs expected TTFT percentiles and token/sec curves. i'll include assumptions about warm cache, quantization level, and instance type.
[00:03:36] [00:03:40] Priya: we also need to define golden prompts for quality checks — if the POC hits latency targets but generates lower quality output, that fails.
[00:03:48] Samira: agreed, add quality gates. we'll ask you to provide a set of 50 gold prompts per class and expected metrics like Rouge/BLEU or human-annotated pass/fail. we can run automated evals during the run.
[00:04:02] Ethan: about measurement — do you recommend replaying real traffic or synthetic loads?
[00:04:09] Diego: replay is best for fidelity (captures token-length distribution, session patterns). synthetic is good for controlled sweeps. our typical plan: replay 48 hours of anonymized traffic at multiple scale factors (1x, 2x, 5x) and also run synthetic sweeps to stress specific tails.
[00:04:26] Samira: and we'll instrument for p50/p90/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT (per-token ms) and measure end-to-end completion for long requests. also track error rates, retries, and queueing times.
[00:04:39] [00:04:45] Maya: how granular should slices be? e.g., by prompt token length buckets?
[00:04:49] Diego: yes — recommended buckets: 0-32 tokens, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048. plus cache-hit vs cache-miss and cold-start vs warm. we'll probably treat the top 1% longest prompts as a separate risk bucket.
[00:05:06] Priya: sounds good. for acceptance criteria, propose: short-chat TTFT p95 < 150ms and p99 < 400ms; long-summary end-to-end p95 < 4s and p99 < 6s. are those acceptable?
[00:05:20] Samira: those are reasonable starting points. i'd make the p99 a bit more lenient initially to avoid noisy failures: p99 450ms for chat, 6.5s for summaries. can we agree to those for the pilot with the caveat we'll refine after initial run?
[00:05:34] Maya: yes, fine.
[00:05:36] [00:05:40] Owen: network egress and VPC peering — we'll need to confirm peering and ensure dedicated pilot capacity. what infra do you need?
[00:05:47] Lina: for dedicated pilot we recommend a 2-week reserved window with dedicated GPU nodes (we'll specify GPU type). minimally, we ask for VPC peering, sample traffic S3 bucket, and a bastion for troubleshooting if on private. for hosted pilot we can do ephemeral instances but TTFT will vary.
[00:06:06] Ethan: we prefer private (VPC) testing for data controls. we'll request SOC2 docs as well.
[00:06:11] Samira: we'll attach SOC2 + SAML docs in the follow-up.
[00:06:15] [00:06:20] Diego: measurement detail — we'll instrument timestamps at: request ingress, routing decision, model load start, first-token emit, each token delta sample, and response close. that lets us compute TTFT and per-token ms distributions. we also capture queuing time in the runtime.
[00:06:36] Maya: will you provide the harness so we can run in our environment?
[00:06:40] Diego: yes, we'll provide a small harness that can replay from an ndjson sample and also a k6 script for synthetic load. the harness will emit traces to your tracing system and to our console for cross-correlation.
[00:06:53] Priya: about cost metrics — we need per-request token cost numbers for budgeting. can you estimate cost per 1000 requests for our mix?
[00:06:59] Diego: yes — the simulation will show overall cost and also show cost sensitivity to batch size and quantization. we'll include a 'cost per 1k reqs' table for the pilot mix.
[00:07:12] [00:07:20] Maya: timeline — we prefer a 2-week pilot starting Aug 16. is that feasible?
[00:07:26] Lina: yes. proposed timeline: this week (Aug 5-7) exchange artifacts (harness, traffic samples). Aug 9-12 run pre-checks and infra setup. Aug 16-30 pilot run. Aug 31 review and decision.
[00:07:42] Samira: agree. we'll also include one mid-pilot checkpoint.
[00:07:46] Owen: on the SLOs — if we fail on p99 by small margins, do we consider partial success? how to grade?
[00:07:54] Samira: we'll propose a graded acceptance: primary SLO is p95; p99 is allowed up to an agreed degradation threshold (e.g., up to 1.2x target) and must be explained by root cause. full pass requires both within thresholds. partial pass could trigger follow-up run after optimization.
[00:08:10] Priya: can you capture that as a pass/fail matrix?
[00:08:13] Diego: yes, i'll include an acceptance matrix in the runbook.
[00:08:17] [00:08:20] Ethan: testing metrics — what percent of traffic should be sampled for tracing?
[00:08:24] Diego: recommend 100% for synthetic and replay (we log) but trace sampling can be 5-20% to limit traces. for tail analysis we'll keep 100% logs for key fields (timestamps, queue time, token counts).
[00:08:39] Maya: security question — will prompts or outputs be stored? we need assurances on redaction and retention.
[00:08:46] Samira: we can configure redaction and short retention for the pilot; by default logs are anonymized and we can disable storing full prompts. we'll attach the data handling runbook.
[00:08:56] [00:09:00] Priya: small nit — you mentioned KV cache impact. how much does a cold cache blow up TTFT?
[00:09:05] Diego: depends. cold KV load can add 30-200ms depending on model and sequence length. that's why we recommend warm-up runs and a warm cache window before measuring TTFT for chat.
[00:09:19] Samira: practical pilot plan: 1) prewarm with 10k synthetic requests to populate caches; 2) replay 48h of traffic at 1x/2x; 3) synthetic sweeps for batch sizing and cold-start injection; 4) collect metrics, produce acceptance report.
[00:09:38] Maya: for the golden prompts we'll include 20 high-priority chat prompts and 15 long-form summarization examples.
[00:09:44] [00:09:50] Owen: network — we'll send peering details by Aug 7.
[00:09:52] Samira: noted.
[00:09:55] Diego: one more technical note — when measuring TPOT, measure token delta across the steady-state region (ignore first 8-16 tokens which may include attention warm-up). that'll give a stable per-token ms estimate.
[00:10:10] Priya: clarification — what's reasonable TPOT for the large open model you plan to use?
[00:10:15] Diego: rough numbers: on a A100-like instance with quantized weights and optimal kernels, TPOT could be ~6-12ms per token for mid-size models; for Llama2-70b style it may be 12-25ms/token depending on sequence length and KV hit. i'll specify expected ranges in the sim.
[00:10:34] [00:10:40] Samira: ok, we have enough to draft the runbook. next steps recap: samira send harness, diego send sim, customer send samples + peering. meeting notes and runbook will be shared.
[00:10:54] Maya: thanks all.
[00:10:56] Samira: any final questions?
[00:10:58] Priya: none from me.
[00:11:00] Owen: none.
[00:11:02] Lina: will follow up with calendar invites for prechecks and pilot kickoff.
[00:11:06] Samira: great, thanks everyone. end.

--- End of call ---
